source_snapshot.title: feat(mcp): enrich Ix MCP tools with structured outputs, semantic annotations, and stronger agent interoperability
source_snapshot.body:
## Summary

`ix mcp` already serves Ix's graph tools to MCP clients. This PR makes that tool surface substantially more useful for agents without rebuilding the MCP server: every advertised tool carries truthful semantic annotations, and the JSON-backed tools return typed structured content instead of a string to re-parse.

## Current upstream baseline

- Upstream `main` at open: `ab823e3` (`fix(view): keep backend scope out of generated script (#412)`).
- The MCP server ships from the existing `#397` implementation, with the `#400` and `#401` hardening already merged. This PR builds on that work rather than recreating it.

## Existing MCP state

- Tools served via the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (`^1.30.0`), kept as-is; no SDK upgrade, no dependency change.
- Hardening already present: structured argv, `--` separation, 16 MiB output cap, timeouts, orphan tracking, single-flight lock ownership, per-command scope-cache invalidation, Windows quoting fixes, stdout/stderr separation.
- Most tools returned only `--format llm` text; no typed results, no annotations.

## Remaining problem

1. **No tool annotations.** Clients could not tell a graph read from a backend mutation, so presentation and routing were guesswork.
2. **No structured results.** `ix_map`, `ix_ingest` and `ix_smells` return a stable JSON object from the backend, but agents received it as a string to re-parse.

## Structured outputs

- `ix_map`, `ix_ingest`, `ix_smells` now expose their parsed JSON object as `structuredContent` and advertise an `outputSchema`.
- The schema asserts "an object" (`z.object({}).passthrough()`) deliberately: the real field shape is backend-defined and versioned, so promising specific fields would break tool calls the moment the backend renames one.
- Fallback is `{}` — never a throw — when a future backend returns a non-object shape; the human-readable text is always preserved.
- The remaining tools return their `--format llm` text, which has no stable object shape worth promising.

## Tool annotations

- Every tool in the catalog carries `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint`, plus `title`.
- Graph reads are read-only and idempotent; `ix_map`, `ix_ingest` and `ix_decide` are destructive (they mutate backend state); only `ix_ingest` is open-world, because its GitHub form reaches an external API.
- The table is keyed by `IX_MCP_TOOL_NAMES`, so the typechecker rejects any tool added to the catalog without a truthful classification.
- Annotations are advisory metadata for clients — not security controls. The enforcement that matters (argv construction, timeouts, output bounds, process cleanup) lives in the runner and is unchanged.

## SDK status

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.30.0` is retained. It already supports `outputSchema`, `structuredContent` and tool annotations. No migration.

## Additional verified invariant improvements

None beyond the above were needed: the `#400`/`#401` regression surface (orphan bookkeeping, lock ownership, Windows quoting, timeout containment, output attribution) is already covered by the existing `mcp-runner.test.ts` suite. This PR adds no runner changes.

## Compatibility

- Text output is preserved for every tool; clients that prefer strings see no difference.
- No new dependencies. No Ix-findings, Freebuff or DeepSeek Harness imports.
- Works with the official TypeScript MCP client; structured content and annotations flow through the standard `tools/list` / `tools/call` surface.

## Testing

- `mcp-annotations.test.ts` — every catalogued tool is classified; mutating tools are destructive/non-idempotent/non-read-only; graph reads are read-only+idempotent; only GitHub ingestion is open-world.
- `mcp-structured-output.test.ts` — parsed JSON surfaces as `structuredContent`; non-JSON output falls back to `{}` without throwing; filtered `ix_smells` candidates are structured; `outputSchema` is advertised only for the verified JSON tools.
- Full MCP suite: 44 tests pass (4 files), plus typecheck.

## Historical links

Earlier MCP implementation and hardening work in the `Alot1z/Ix-remap` development fork:

- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/36c7c7eccd8068d48df4f61394b42a3ffa62483c — `feat(mcp): add ix mcp subcommand exposing the code graph as MCP tools (#219)`
- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/66111917a2a58437c91372616f98928876121395 — `fix(mcp): abort in-flight calls on EOF, add ix_read tool, executor timeout coverage`
- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/1a5b0b93c9e8871610370c0f36212be8f6cf6980 — `fix(mcp): harden the stdio server — line-size cap, tree-kill, protocol-abuse matrix (#219)`
- https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/606f18f7ca1a69f4b8ede7c27c1079b024297856 — `docs(mcp): document the hardening contract`

The upstream `#397` MCP PR and `#400`/`#401` hardening PRs merged that lineage into `ix-infrastructure/Ix`; this PR extends the merged result.

@josephismikhail @KageBinary — linking the earlier #219/#397 history and prior fork implementation here so the architectural lineage is straightforward to review.

## Ix-findings evidence

- MCP overview: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/
- MCP architecture: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/implementation/
- MCP security: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/security/
- MCP tests: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/mcp/tests/
- Original issue #219: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/issues/219/
- Historical fork branch: https://alot1z.github.io/Ix-findings/entities/branch-fork-ix-mcp/

## Relationship to PR2

PR2 (`feat/agent: unify Ix context, provenance, and investigation workflows for agents`) adds a deterministic bounded context layer on top of the same graph surface. PR1's annotations tell agents which calls are safe to repeat; PR2's context bundles give agents the answer in one bounded call. They are independent branches against `main`.

commits.message:
feat(mcp): annotate MCP tools with semantic hints

Classify every advertised tool with readOnly/destructive/idempotent/openWorld
hints so MCP clients can present and route them correctly. Graph reads are
read-only and idempotent; ix_map/ix_ingest/ix_decide are destructive; only
ix_ingest is open-world because it reaches GitHub. The table is keyed by the
tool catalog, so the typechecker rejects an unclassified addition. Hints are
advisory client metadata, not security controls — the runner's hardening is
unchanged.

feat(mcp): expose structured output for JSON-backed tools

Return parsed JSON objects as structuredContent for ix_map, ix_ingest, and
ix_smells — the tools whose --format=json output is a verified object — with
an object outputSchema that deliberately asserts only "an object" so backend
field drift cannot break tool calls. The human-readable text result is
preserved for clients that prefer it. Pro tools stay text-only because their
command implementations live in the separate @ix/pro package and their output
shape cannot be verified from this repository.

docs(mcp): document structured results and tool annotations

Record the semantic hints on every tool and the structuredContent/outputSchema
behavior of ix_map, ix_ingest, and ix_smells in the MCP consolidation doc, so
plugin consumers and reviewers know what the server advertises.
